vulnerability.title: Django archive.extract allows directory traversal when extracting tar/zip project templates supplied to startproject/startapp --template
vulnerability.category_l2: directory traversal via absolute member paths and dot segments in tar/zip template archives

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag 3.0.2 peels to a3697439; its django/utils/archive.py blob 235809f2 is byte-identical at 3.0.11 and 3.1, and differs at 3.0.12 (d5a0cf04), while the 3.0.x fix 52e409ed is absent from 3.0.11 and an ancestor of 3.0.12

critical_operation.description: TarArchive.extract iterates the archive members and builds the destination path as os.path.join(to_path, name) with no containment check. os.path.join discards to_path when name is absolute ('/tmp/evil.py'), and dot segments ('../../evil') survive the optional leading-directory stripping, so the joined path resolves outside the extraction directory. The method then creates directories and writes the member contents with open(filename, 'wb'), giving an attacker-controlled archive arbitrary file writes with the privileges of the developer running startproject/startapp --template (the caller extracts into a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp directory). ZipArchive.extract (line 201 at 3.0.2) contains the identical join and is the same defect for zip templates. The fix adds BaseArchive.target_filename(), which applies os.path.abspath to both paths and raises SuspiciousOperation when the result does not start with the extraction root, and routes both extract methods through it; the zip path additionally skips empty names and tests name (not filename) for a trailing separator.

entry_point.description: The public django.utils.archive.extract(path, to_path) opens the archive through Archive(path) and delegates to the format-specific extract; startproject/startapp --template reach it through TemplateCommand.handle_template/extract.

trace.description: TemplateCommand.handle_template accepts a file path or URL and calls self.extract(absolute_path) for a template archive
TemplateCommand.extract creates a tempfile.mkdtemp directory and calls archive.extract(filename, tempdir)
TarArchive.extract joins the unchecked member name to the extraction root and writes the file
ZipArchive.extract performs the identical unchecked join for zip templates

location.verification_method: Static read of archive.py at 3.0.2, 3.0.11, 3.0.12, 2.2.17 and 2.2.18, of the 3.0.x/2.2.x fix and test diffs and of the 3.0.12 release notes; git blob identity and tag ancestry were checked against a local clone. No archive was extracted and no test suite run.

field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.

families: upstream git history and release tags
source_crosscheck.notes: The Django announcement, NVD, OSV/GHSA and the fixed tags agree on the three ranges (2.2 <2.2.18, 3.0 <3.0.12, 3.1 <3.1.6) and on the root cause in django.utils.archive.extract. NVD assigns CWE-22 and CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM; the Django advisory labels the issue severity "low" and GHSA labels it MODERATE. The MITRE CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS). OSV's GIT range events again name unrelated security-archive documentation commits as introduced and the release tag commits as fixed, so fix verification used the five vendor-listed changesets and git ancestry instead.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read TarArchive.extract and ZipArchive.extract at 3.0.2 and confirm that os.path.join(to_path, name) is unchecked for absolute names and dot segments.
An independent reviewer must confirm 52e409ed is absent from 3.0.2 and 3.0.11 and an ancestor of 3.0.12, and that 3.0.12 archive.py routes both extract methods through target_filename.
An independent reviewer must confirm the 3.1.6 and 2.2.18 fixes and the three release boundaries against a second source family.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No malicious archive was built or extracted and no Django test suite was executed; the finding is static.

Exploitation requires the developer to pass an attacker-controlled archive (or URL) to startproject/startapp --template; this is a supply-chain/developer-workstation vector, not a remotely reachable web endpoint.
The MITRE CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS).
NVD also carries a CVSS 2.0 metric of 5.0 (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N); the canonical score follows the NVD primary CVSS 3.1 metric.
The Django advisory's qualitative severity is "low" while NVD rates 5.3 MEDIUM and GHSA labels the issue MODERATE; the qualitative labels are recorded as source disagreement, not reconciled.

OSV's GIT range events are conversion artifacts: introduced events are later documentation commits (2a62cdcf, 2a04e24d, 0b8a0296) and fixed events are the 2.2.18/3.0.12/3.1.6 release commits; they were not used as fix evidence.

Static observation, confirmed by a later vendor fix: the 2021 check compares filename.startswith(target_path) without a path-separator boundary, so a member resolving to a sibling directory whose name shares the prefix (for example /tmp/extract vs /tmp/extract_evil) passes. Django re-fixed this as CVE-2025-59682 in commit 924a0c092e65fa2d0953fd1855d2dc8786d94de2 (2025-10-01, follow-up to 05413afa), replacing startswith with os.path.commonpath and shipping in 4.2.25/5.1.13/5.2.7. This affects the fixed code, not the 3.0.2 vulnerable code.
No downstream distribution backport (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Oracle, NetApp) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.
The snapshot inventory status is NEEDS_REVIEW with 67 ambiguous files, not a clean PASS.
open_questions: Whether startproject/startapp template archives are commonly fetched from untrusted sources was not surveyed.

Whether Python's tarfile/zipfile path sanitisation or CPython's os.path.join behaviour changed across supported interpreter versions was not traced; only the documented os.path.join absolute-path override and dot-segment semantics are relied on.
The sibling-prefix weakness in target_filename() is recorded as an observation; whether it is exploitable in a given deployment was not tested.
